A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemCast. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison despite reorganization and revised experimental reporting.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting results on ten datasets in Table 2, ablations and sensitivity studies, and qualitative forecasting and failure analyses in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting experiments, including revised results in Tables 2–3, ablations, sensitivity studies, and the appendix's qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The hierarchical memory, composite retrieval, trajectory selection, reflection, and confidence adaptation procedures are retained. New Section 3.3 explains the textual memory representation already present in v1; the reorganized accumulation, utilization, and evolution sections do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten datasets: NP, PJM, BE, FR, DE, ETTh1, ETTm1, WP, SP, and MOPEX. The OOD oil-temperature case and appendix failure scenarios are also retained. Revised split counts do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eleven baselines, including TimeXer, LLM-Time, TimeReasoner, and Time-LLM. The backbone and aggregation comparisons also retain their participants. Newly cited memory systems are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix Table 7 revises every dataset's reported train/validation/test counts. EPF splits change from (10224,1584,3024) to (10147,1450,2899); ETTh1/MOPEX from (8544,1344,2544) to (7344,2448,2448); and ETTm1/WP/SP from (16896,2496,4896) to (14457,4820,4819). This substantially changes the documented protocol, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Horizons, metrics, and normalization policy remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The memory-component ablation in Table 3 changes its DE full-model reference, altering the reported gaps against unchanged removal variants. The remaining confidence, aggregation, backbone, context, and sensitivity analyses, together with the OOD and appendix failure cases, are retained without new analytical questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained trajectory sampling and memory-confidence mechanisms do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting for the experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises comparator scores and rankings while retaining every MemCast value. For example, TimeReasoner's SP MSE changes from 17.599 to 27.551 against MemCast's unchanged 22.998, and its ETTm MSE changes from 1.574 to 4.038 against 3.999, reversing both rankings. TimeXer, LLM-Time, and Time-LLM entries also change. Table 3 changes MemCast's DE MSE/MAE from 282.801/10.903 to 210.445/9.195. With revised split descriptions, these are reported-result revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The problem definition, similarity formulation, memory thresholds, and trajectory-selection rule are retained. Renaming the DTW denominator from tau to gamma and explaining its scaling role clarify overloaded notation without establishing different mathematics. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: forecasting through hierarchical experience memory, experience-conditioned reasoning, and confidence adaptation without claimed test-data leakage. Their broad effectiveness claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 substantially revise interpretations. The blanket comparison against TimeReasoner is qualified; PJM's memory ablation now emphasizes historical patterns, while ETTh emphasizes wisdom and patterns over laws. The contextual-feature discussion reverses its emphasis from static to dynamic context for PJM/ETTh and acknowledges the NP MAE exception. Claims of consistently better performance from stronger backbones are also tempered. Appendix failure limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly describes textual memory encoding, updates after ground truth becomes available, and bounded memory maintenance in Sections 3.3, 3.6, and 4.1. Conversely, v1's zero initialization and explicit confidence-plus-similarity selection condition are omitted. API settings, hardware, code access, and the substantive Appendix A.4 prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning through human, recurrent, external, compressed, and LLM memory, including MemoRAG, Memory3, and HippoRAG. Section 3.3 additionally contrasts textual experience with dense-vector, key-value, and file-based memory, extending well beyond v1's two forecasting-related literature subsections.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting spans the introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental discussion. Methodology is reorganized around encoding, accumulation, utilization, and evolution. Appendix failure terminology and cross-references are corrected, and correspondence, publication, acknowledgements, and conflict-disclosure text are updated or added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is relabeled and regrouped to match the revised methodological organization. Existing figures and tables are repositioned, including placing Figures 3–4 together; table emphasis and some captions are revised. The same seven tables and eight figures remain, with the appendix forecast and failure plots retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves interpretive accuracy by aligning the memory and contextual-feature discussion with Tables 3–5 and acknowledging exceptions previously obscured by broad claims. The DE ablation reference now agrees with Table 2, and expanded memory positioning and feedback timing improve clarity. These gains outweigh limited losses in confidence-update detail, but unexplained split and baseline-score revisions prevent treating the revision as substantially stronger empirical validation.
